item.title: Putin Looks to FSB Hardliners to Keep His Wartime Elite in Line
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: Many of Russia’s elite increasingly fear the Federal Security Service is out of control as President Vladimir Putin tasks the agency with maintaining his grip on power amid growing unease over the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Oil Climbs as Strait of Hormuz Deal Prospects Unclear
item.content:encoded: Oil extended gains after a report that Iran attacked "hostile targets" in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian media also reported that Tehran will seek to bar US and Israeli ships from the waterway. Bloomberg's Yongchang Chin reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Ally Ogles Defeated in Tennessee Congressional GOP Primary
item.author: John Harney
item.content:encoded: Representative Andy Ogles of Tennessee, a fervent ally of Donald Trump, lost a Republican primary on Thursday night, despite a tele-rally and other gestures of support by the president.

item.title: Our Town Episode 1 Bloomberg Podcast Series
item.content:encoded: Oh, the things you can find with an inquisitive mind – and a metal detector.

item.title: Congo Ebola Outbreak: Merck Ervebo Vaccine, Gilead Remdesivir Eyed for Wider Use
item.author: Janice Kew and Jason Gale
item.content:encoded: Merck & Co.’s Ebola vaccine and an antiviral drug from Gilead Sciences Inc. are set for wider use in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo to blunt the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record.

item.title: Indian Students Face Online Harassment Weeks After Protests End
item.author: Akriti Sharma
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s olive branch to the young people behind India’s biggest student-led protests in years has done little to stem the online abuse and police action many participants say they continue to face.

item.title: Malaysia Delays Charge Against Ex-PM After Hospitalization
item.author: Kok Leong Chan
item.content:encoded: A Malaysian court postponed proceedings to charge former Prime Minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob with failing to declare his assets after he was admitted to a heart hospital following questioning by the country’s anti-graft agency.

item.title: Judge Dismisses Former Olympian’s Felony Charge in Reflecting Pool Case
item.author: Chris Cameron
item.content:encoded: The move ends the criminal case for David Hearn, a former Olympic canoeist, after prosecutors acknowledged that the Trump administration’s claims of vandalism were false.

item.title: Edgy Vanity Plates Test Limits of Free Speech
item.author: Adam Liptak
item.content:encoded: Virginia will ask the Supreme Court to hear a dispute over a seven-character license plate message.

item.title: Who Will Inherit the MAGA Movement in 2028? | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/06/2026
item.content:encoded: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. Republican Senator Kevin Cramer of North Dakota says lawmakers’ first priority is passing a continuing resolution to fund the government through December 11. On Republican holdouts over Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney general, Cramer says he is hopeful President Donald Trump could weigh in and persuade them to support his nominee. House Minority Whip Katherine Clark (D-MA) says progressive Abdul Ed-Sayed's win in Michigan is a signal that voters are looking for "fighters" who will stand up for them in Congress. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Affordability is Top Issue for Midterms: Rep. Clark
item.content:encoded: House Minority Whip Katherine Clark (D-MA) says progressive Abdul Ed-Sayed's win in Michigan is a signal that voters are looking for "fighters" who will stand up for them in Congress. She says she believes Democrats will have the majority in the House come November, while signaling openness to a stopgap bill to avert a shutdown, noting that the Senate's proposal is a "big improvement." She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sen. Cramer: Funding Vote Is Senate’s Top Priority
item.content:encoded: With just one day left in the Senate’s session before a scheduled August recess, Republican Senator Kevin Cramer of North Dakota says lawmakers’ first priority is passing a continuing resolution to fund the government through December 11. On Republican holdouts over Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney general, Cramer says he is hopeful President Donald Trump could weigh in and persuade them to support his nominee. He also says regular conversations between Trump and Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh are appropriate, noting it would be “strange” if they weren’t speaking somewhat regularly, as long as the central bank remains independent. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Missile Test Near Tuvalu Raises Tsunami Concerns Among Pacific Nations
item.author: Ainsley Thomson
item.content:encoded: A meeting of Pacific Island nations has failed to reach consensus on criticizing a Chinese missile test a month ago, underscoring the geopolitical tensions that are becoming starker in the region.

item.title: Warsh's Next Moves & Situational Awareness' New Bet | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/6/2026
item.content:encoded: Economics and Policy Correspondent Mike McKee & Senior Federal Reserve Reporter Enda Curran react to reports regarding President Trump's relationship and communications with Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, plus a preview of July payrolls dropping Friday. Then, Bloomberg Hedge Fund Reporter Hema Parmar reports what $400 Million bet Situational Awareness made in its return back to investing. Plus, Bloomberg Intelligence's Global Head of Technology Research Mandeep Singh talks Alphabet's potentially $25 Billion bond sale. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Administration Considers Order on Autism and Vaccines
item.author: Rachel Cohrs Zhang, Riley Griffin and Skylar Woodhouse
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration is actively considering issuing an executive order on vaccines and autism as soon as next week, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Trump Tries to Curb Birthright Citizenship After Court Loss
item.author: Skylar Woodhouse
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump signed a pair of executive orders aimed at denying citizenship to certain people born in the US, his second attempt to curb birthright citizenship after the Supreme Court knocked down an earlier directive.

item.title: Trump Order Sets 15% Tariff, Price Floors on Polysilicon Imports
item.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump ordered new tariffs as well as price floors on imported polysilicon used in semiconductors and solar panels, warning that US reliance on foreign supplies threatens national security.

item.title: Trump May Net Tax Windfall in Crypto Bill Divestiture Plan
item.author: Lydia Beyoud, Olga Kharif and Steven T. Dennis
item.content:encoded: The bipartisan ethics proposal senators have pitched to President Donald Trump to get landmark crypto legislation over the line in Congress could trigger a significant tax benefit for the president: the ability to defer capital gains levies on his crypto holdings.

item.title: DOJ Says Duke Law School Discriminated in Admissions
item.author: Liam Knox
item.content:encoded: The Justice Department said Thursday it has found Duke University School of Law discriminated against applicants based on race, the Trump administration’s latest move in its wide-ranging higher education pressure campaign.

item.title: Hemp Fight Snarls Speedy Passage of Government Funding Bill
item.author: Catie Edmondson and Olivia Diaz
item.content:encoded: A White House effort to delay a ban on intoxicating hemp was holding up a final agreement on a bipartisan spending bill ahead of a monthlong Senate recess.

item.title: Women’s Share of Top Military Promotions Falls as Hegseth Blocks Nominees
item.author: C.J. Robinson
item.content:encoded: The percentage of high-ranking officer nominations going to women is currently at its lowest level in over two decades.

item.title: Iran Wants to Bar US, Israeli Ships From Hormuz in Peace Accord
item.author: Eltaf Najafizada, Sara Gharaibeh, Skylar Woodhouse and Sonya Dymova
item.content:encoded: Iran will seek to bar US and Israeli ships from the Strait of Hormuz and require compensation from hostile countries before they’re allowed to sail through it, according to local media reports on a proposed Iran-Oman deal to manage the crucial waterway.

item.title: Houthis Carry Out Deadly Attack in Yemen and Hit Saudi Territory
item.author: Sara Gharaibeh and Sherif Tarek
item.content:encoded: The Houthis conducted a “large-scale” attack against forces from Yemen’s Saudi-backed government, and struck the southwestern Saudi region of Najran, raising concerns over a widening of the US-Israeli war on Iran into a broader conflict.

item.title: Moderate Democrats Prepare for ‘War’ Against an Ascendant Left
item.author: Shane Goldmacher
item.content:encoded: One moderate group says the progressive wins are “deeply troubling” and is planning a $15 million effort against democratic socialism.

item.title: Insults, Expletives and Fat-Shaming: Vance Trolls Critics on the Right and Left
item.author: Peter Baker

item.title: Tennessee’s Andy Ogles Faces Well-Funded Opposition in House Primary Thursday
item.author: Patricia Mazzei, Tim Balk and Emily Cochrane
item.content:encoded: Representative Andy Ogles received President Trump’s endorsement, but his challenger, Charlie Hatcher, a former state agriculture commissioner, has the backing of Gov. Bill Lee.

item.title: Senate Panel Has Obtained Copy of Fauci’s Government Cellphone
item.author: Sheryl Gay Stolberg
item.content:encoded: The development comes as a Senate committee prepares to vote Thursday on whether to hold Dr. Anthony S. Fauci in contempt of Congress for refusing to answer questions at a hearing.

item.title: Xi Flexes Growing Legal Arsenal to Warn Trump Before Summit
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: China’s latest barrage of countermeasures against the US drew on an expanding legal arsenal, demonstrating Beijing’s growing capacity to retaliate while warning Washington against further tech curbs before Xi Jinping’s expected visit next month.

item.title: A Growing Number of Election Deniers Hold Key Local Roles in Midterms
item.author: Nick Corasaniti and Alexandra Berzon

item.title: F.D.A. Approves Moderna’s mRNA Flu Vaccine

item.content:encoded: The agency had initially refused to even review the application but reversed course after a public outcry.

item.title: Federal Judge Weakens The National Firearms Act
item.author: Chris Cameron
item.content:encoded: The National Firearms Act mandated a permitting process for short-barreled rifles and shotguns, as well as suppressors. A judge ruled that the provision was unconstitutional.
